title: Predicate Boundary of a Dictator Test
statement: Let $\Psi$ be a finite family of predicates on signs, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\alpha<\beta\le 1$, and let $e:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ take $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$ and tend to $0$ as its argument tends to $0$ through positive values. Suppose a family of randomized testers, one for each positive cube dimension, uses only predicates in $\Psi$; accepts every coordinate dictator with probability at least $\beta$; and accepts every function with all stable influences at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$ for each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$. For every positive dimension, the tester's allowed predicate family is finite and every check selected by any seed uses a predicate in that family.
hypotheses_covered: Every tester check uses a predicate in $\Psi$
Every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$
For each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, functions whose stable influences are all at most $\varepsilon$ are accepted with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$
